note: Real incidents from Sept 2026. Each must be answered by proving the cause before any posting. Expected outcomes describe what a correct agent concludes; the live data may have moved on, so graders check the reasoning and the book/flag decision, not exact current balances.

evals.name: tokenless-network-credit
evals.prompt: Stripe AED 785.79 awaiting payout, bank ref FT26267TVX45 2026-09-24, narration Inward Telex Payment/NETWORK INTERNATIONAL LLC/...BATCB1muf2v44411/IPPCG1muf4hlma00/...\HCP. No file uploaded. The reference doesn't say stripe, fetch it from the stripe api.
evals.expected_output: Checks both Stripe payouts and Shopify Payments payouts for an exact 785.79 match; finds it is Shopify Payments UAE payout 149110423710, not Stripe. Does not upload or force a Stripe match.
assertions: Considers Shopify Payments as well as Stripe for a Network International credit without a rail token
Matches on exact amount, not a tolerance window
Does not book or force-match to a Stripe payout

evals.name: split-charges-one-payout
evals.prompt: WA55596 has 1 invoice (MNS-052851, AED 1,024.00) and the drawer says the gateway amount is 341.34. Plug all the stripe payments to that invoice.
evals.expected_output: Finds three Stripe charges of 341.34 described WA55596 (via charges search by amount), all in payout po_1UCqGq; recognises the payout rows were stored with one charge; re-syncs the payout so the order row is 1,024.02; dry-runs one payment of 1,024.00 plus fee and 0.02 difference; posts only after the dry run is clean.
assertions: Proves the charges sum to the invoice before booking
Fixes the stored payout rows (re-sync) rather than forcing a partial amount
Runs a dry run before posting
Books a single payment for the full invoice

evals.name: order-across-two-payouts
evals.prompt: WA55612 shows 'invoice 2,557 doesn't match gateway 70.00' on one Stripe credit and 'doesn't match 2,487.00' on another. Close it.
evals.expected_output: Notes 70 + 2,487 = 2,557 exactly with a single open invoice; applies each part to the same invoice through the force-allocation route dated on its own credit; books each part's fee via publishSettlements.
assertions: Verifies the parts sum exactly to one open invoice
Uses per-settlement force allocations rather than one combined raw payment
Books the fees through the normal engine

evals.name: booked-but-deleted-in-zoho
evals.prompt: For some shopify orders the fee wasn't booked — ledger shows the customer payment for 3470 (MNS-052927, FT26253GNVQV, 744.00) but no fee. The drawer says booked.
evals.expected_output: Reads the stored fee expense id and confirms via Zoho that it no longer exists (404); explains it was deleted in Zoho after posting (not by the revert flow); re-posts the fee through the engine without re-posting the payment.
assertions: Checks the stored Zoho document exists instead of trusting the local booked flag
Does not post a second customer payment

evals.name: mismatch-must-flag
evals.expected_output: Finds invoice MNS-052666 3,035.00 vs Stripe 3,058.19 (overpaid 23.19); does not force it; flags the bank credit for review with both amounts and the signed gap.
assertions: Does not post a payment for a real amount mismatch
Flags the credit with both amounts and the signed gap

evals.name: paid-by-hand-then-refunded
evals.expected_output: Finds the invoice already paid by hand (4,442.07), the Stripe sale 4,434.18 on one payout and refund 4,244.71 on another with credit note OCN-03558 already refunded; holds it and flags the fee and the 189.47 kept as decisions for the founder.
assertions: Recognises the invoice was paid outside Omnia
Does not post a payment or refund
Flags with the specific decisions needed
